lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the project Asplenium through clathrate stem scales and long linear/lunate sori with one-sided true indusia, then contrast that reproductive pattern with the round sori of the other project fern families.

taxonomy_scope.project_teaching_treatment: Regional/FNA-style narrow Aspleniaceae for field learning.
taxonomy_scope.current_kew_note: POWO 2026 uses a broader Aspleniaceae that synonymizes Thelypteridaceae into Aspleniaceae. This learner retains the FNA-style Thelypteridaceae module as a practical regional teaching unit and labels the alternative circumscription explicitly.

project_scope.note: The current project pool contains Asplenium resiliens. The species is accepted by current Kew and native to Texas.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Turn the frond over. Look for elongate to linear sori lying along veins, usually each covered by a narrow true indusium attached along one side. Then inspect the stem/rhizome scales for a clathrate, stained-glass-like cell pattern.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Ferns with monomorphic fronds in the project concept. Stem scales are characteristically clathrate; frond division varies widely across the family.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Sori are commonly lunate to linear and borne on veins; true indusia usually mirror the sorus shape and attach along one side.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Linear sori + one-sided true indusium is the fastest practical spleenwort cue; do not rely on frond shape alone.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole frond → black stipe/rachis → linear sori → one-sided true indusium → clathrate scale → round-sorus family comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Spleenworts become much easier when the underside of the frond is treated like a map. The sori are long lines instead of round dots.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the black-stemmed spleenwort silhouette
steps.look_for: A narrow 1-pinnate blade with many small pinnae and a glossy black stipe and rachis.
steps.why_it_matters: This gives the crew a fast field gestalt before the reproductive confirmation.

steps.title: 2 · Flip a fertile pinna over
steps.look_for: Several narrow elongate sori arranged along veins on each pinna.
steps.why_it_matters: Linear sori are the highest-value visible family clue in the regional Aspleniaceae concept.

steps.title: 3 · Find the true indusium
steps.look_for: A narrow membrane attached along one side of each sorus and opening toward the other side.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates Asplenium from Polypodiaceae, whose sori lack a true indusium, and from local Pteridaceae false-indusium patterns.

steps.title: 4 · Zoom into a clathrate scale
steps.look_for: Dark radial walls and clearer tangential walls forming a lattice or stained-glass pattern.
steps.why_it_matters: FNA identifies clathrate scales plus linear indusiate sori as a strong Aspleniaceae combination.

steps.title: 5 · Limestone habitat is supporting evidence
steps.look_for: A. resiliens commonly grows on limestone or other basic rock.
steps.why_it_matters: Useful Central Texas context, but habitat never replaces the sorus characters.

comparisons.title: Aspleniaceae vs Polypodiaceae
comparisons.rule: Asplenium has linear/lunate sori with a true one-sided indusium. Pleopeltis has round sori without a true indusium and conspicuous peltate scales on the lower blade.

comparisons.title: Aspleniaceae vs Thelypteridaceae (regional/FNA treatment)
comparisons.rule: Asplenium has linear sori and clathrate stem scales; Thelypteris has round sori, commonly reniform indusia, and conspicuous hairs/glands on the frond.

comparisons.title: Aspleniaceae vs Pteridaceae
comparisons.rule: Local cliffbrake-type Pteridaceae often carries sori at the blade margin beneath a rolled false indusium; Asplenium sori sit along veins away from the margin under a separate true indusium.

visual_lesson.caveat: Family circumscription differs among modern references. Current Kew uses a broad Aspleniaceae that includes Thelypteridaceae, while Flora of North America retains them as separate families. The learner shows both frameworks rather than hiding the disagreement.

genera.fast_cue: narrow 1-pinnate fern + dark glossy rachis + linear indusiate sori

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted by current Kew; FNA also recognizes the species.
